name: Just Enough
problem: Most casual puzzle games repeat one mechanic with escalating difficulty and offer no sense of daily shared ritual.
solution: Designed and built a solo mobile puzzle game around a single constraint (removal only), spanning 10 distinct mechanics, a daily shared puzzle, and adaptive difficulty.
outcome: Shipped an Expo/React Native app end to end solo: game design, level generation logic, Firebase auth/data, crash reporting, and store distribution.

story.hook: Every level starts overloaded. The only move is letting go.

stages.title: Too Much, Not Too Hard
stages.copy: Most casual puzzle games repeat one mechanic with escalating difficulty and offer no sense of daily shared ritual.

stages.title: One Rule: Remove
stages.copy: Every level starts overloaded — a cluttered desk, a list of numbers with a hidden rule, a grid that looks solved until you check twice. Removal is the only tool.

stages.title: Ten Mechanics, One Constraint
stages.copy: Grid logic, number chains, memory match, and NYT-Connections-style categorizing all share the same core move, so the game stays varied without losing its identity.

stages.title: Built to Adapt
stages.copy: Designed and built solo around a single constraint, spanning 10 distinct mechanics, a daily shared puzzle, and difficulty that adjusts to who's playing.

stages.title: Worlds That Unlock
stages.copy: Levels are grouped into worlds that open up as you clear the ones before them, each with its own painted backdrop and tone.

stages.title: Shipped End to End
stages.copy: Shipped an Expo/React Native app solo: game design, level generation logic, Firebase auth/data, crash reporting, and store distribution.

name: BazaarX
problem: The existing experience needed clearer positioning, stronger visual hierarchy, and a more confident path to action.
solution: Designed a focused digital experience with responsive UI, clear sections, visual rhythm, and interaction details that support the user journey.
outcome: Adds a portfolio-ready case study that can be routed into the right Saathvik Visuals curation room automatically.
